The San Jose Earthquakes hosted Orlando City SC in an MLS clash that promised high intensity from the opening whistle. The atmosphere at the stadium was electric on 2026-07-23 as both teams looked to secure crucial points in the league standings. Orlando's Explosive Start Orlando City SC wasted no time establishing their dominance on the pitch. In just the 7th minute, David Brekalo found the back of the net, clinical in his finish after being set up by a brilliant pass from Eduard Atuesta . The playmaker Atuesta was the architect of the visitors' attack, and he delivered again in the 29th minute, providing the assist for Ivan Angulo to double the lead. As the San Jose Earthquakes struggled to find their rhythm, the match grew physical, leading to yellow cards for Atuesta and later Timo Werner just before the halftime whistle. Griezmann and Continued Dominance The second half began exactly where the first left off. Only three minutes after the restart, Antoine Griezmann extended the lead in the 48th minute, converting a chance created by Justin Ellis . The San Jose Earthquakes found themselves under constant pressure, with Ronaldo Vieira and Preston Judd both receiving yellow cards as they tried to halt the opposition's momentum. In the 73rd minute, Braian Ojeda added a fourth goal to the tally, once again assisted by the tireless Eduard Atuesta , who completed a remarkable hat-trick of assists. Following the goal, a series of substitutions followed for both sides, including the introduction of Paul Marie , Darius Johnson , and Ian Harkes . Despite some late defensive caution that saw Harvey Sarajian and Daniel Munie cautioned, the visitors comfortably controlled the final stages until the referee brought an end to a commanding performance.

Orlando City SC and Philadelphia Union faced off on May 13, 2026, in a fixture that promised to be a significant test for both squads in the MLS campaign. The atmosphere was electric as both sets of players took to the field, knowing that every moment could be crucial in such a high-stakes encounter. Orlando Sets the Pace The match began with high intensity, and it did not take long for the deadlock to be broken. Following an early yellow card for goalkeeper Andrew Rick , Orlando City SC earned a penalty in the 19th minute. Martin Ojeda stepped up and coolly converted from the spot to give the home side the lead. The momentum stayed with the hosts, and in the 27th minute, Griffin Dorsey doubled the advantage to 2-0, finishing precisely and leaving Philadelphia Union with a mountain to climb before the half-hour mark. Philadelphia Responds and Tactical Shifts In the second half, the game’s dynamic shifted dramatically. Philadelphia Union emerged from the break with renewed intent and managed to pull a goal back in the 54th minute when Milan Iloski found the net following a decisive pass from Nathan Harriel . The contest grew more physical, resulting in yellow cards for Tiago Carvalho , Danley Jean Jacques , and Jeremy Rafanello . Both managers looked to refresh their lineups through substitutions, with the introductions of Cavan Sullivan , Duncan McGuire , and Tyrese Spicer proving pivotal to the unfolding drama. Late Drama and the Decisive Blow The final twenty minutes were defined by a stunning sequence of goals. In the 72nd minute, substitute Duncan McGuire made it 3-1 after being set up by Tyrese Spicer , seemingly putting the result beyond doubt. However, Philadelphia Union struck back instantly; Cavan Sullivan scored in the 75th minute, and just four minutes later, Ben Bender restored parity following an assist from Stas Korzeniowski . Just as a draw seemed certain, Orlando City SC launched one final assault. In the 90th minute, Martin Ojeda secured his second goal of the night assisted by Adrian Marin , clinching a dramatic 4-3 victory in one of the season's most thrilling encounters.
